title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A mobile trading app was compromised by scammers who overlaid fake account information on users' screens. The victims saw false balances and transaction confirmations that made fraudulent investments appear legitimate, allowing the scammers to gain trust and extract larger sums before the scheme collapsed at withdrawal time. The underlying app itself was legitimate, but the AI-generated overlay created a false reality the user had no way to verify against ground truth.

This is a case of impersonation and deception at the point of deployment, where the scam operated within the normal user interface rather than requiring technical compromise of the app's core systems. A retired couple lost nearly $800,000 because they trusted visual evidence on their own device, evidence that had been systematically falsified. Catching this would have required either independent verification of account balances outside the app, or security systems that authenticated the legitimacy of visual overlays before displaying them.

It is not established whether the trading app's developers were aware of the overlay attack, whether they assisted the scammers, or what steps they took to detect or prevent such manipulation.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to download a mobile trading app and begin investing small amounts of money. After seeing modest returns and being able to withdraw funds initially, Jerry's trust grew and he increased his investments. However, when he tried to withdraw a larger sum last week, the transaction failed and he contacted authorities.

Police determined that while the trading app was legitimate, scammers had created a fake AI-generated overlay that showed false account balances and transactions on Jerry's screen. The couple lost their entire life savings to the elaborate scheme. Though Gwinnett County police are investigating, authorities say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. The Dunaways are speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers, and their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them with daily expenses.
